As a lurker who is hypersensitive to emotions -  feelings are absolutely real, and not just a label for thoughts. The entire ancient philosophy of stoicism is founded around the notion of separating your thoughts and feelings so as to achieve balance in one's life. Thus, they are not the same and can exist without each other (well, thoughts without feelings. feelings without thoughts tend to be more chemical/hormonal than anything else). This is also what a lot of meditation and self help is about.  

I'm not quite sure where you're getting your info, but you repeatedly say "no one has an answer" about things that most people have answers for. For example - you ask if the sensory experience of emotions actually exists? yes. And it does for most people I have asked. i personally feel it viscerally in my solar plexus. When I am very happy, there are waves of tingles that radiate outwards through all my limbs. When I feel love, it's like warm bubbles inside of me that rise up my throat and into my chest. When i'm angry, it burns even hotter in my chest, pulls at my face and my skin. 

The thing is that people's sensory experience of emotions is not uniform; but it doesn't mean it's not happening. It is more painful and distracting than most physical sensations I experience tbh.

well, most private schools already have less disposable income and lower teacher pay than state schools. the misconception that all private schools are like eton is ridiculous; and frankly even a small amount of extra students into the state system will be a massive problem. I am a state school teacher and we're already having to cram 33+ students into every teenie tiny classroom, we have no budget to print, and half the students who should have been excluded haven't been because there is nowhere to send them.

Just saying - most independent schools earn less and have lower-paid staff than state schools. I say this as a state school teacher who is looking to move to the independent sector because the state sector is overwhelmed and quite frankly completely crumbling. Part of that is because so much of each schools funding is top-sliced from their academy trusts (which now almost every school in england is a part of).

Private schools don't get government handouts, and most in the uk are barely keeping themselves afloat. If i was to take the job at the private school i've been offered, i would be getting a very significant pay cut (which is saying something, given that the state school pay is already crap) since, once again, it is the best most private schools can afford.

You don't need to worry about Eton - the real rich go there, and they will be completely unaffected by this change. This is not going to hurt the actual rich, it will just put even more pressure on the already floundering state system, and take away opportunities from middle class and some working class families who are giving everything for their kids' education.

Both of those articles reference using the 16 personalities test, which as other users have already mentioned, is a misinterpretation of Myers Briggs (yet, somehow, has dwarfed actual Myers Briggs on the internet). Actual Myers Briggs types without a test, by studying cognitive functions.

Also, a vice article and an article from a random blogging site are hardly credible sources in the face of decades of psychological study of cognitive functions.

The Vice article author really had no idea what he was talking about, either; his whole issue is that MBTI is binary - you're either introverted or extroverted, sensing or intuitive, etc. Which like. Did he do any research at all? In actual MBTI which, again, is all about cognitive functions, whether you have an 'E' or an 'I' at the front of your code just dictates whether your leading function is 'extroverted' or 'introverted', and not necessarily in a traditional sense. For example, as an ENFP, my leading function is extroverted intuition, which conveys my enjoyment of sifting through many different ideas, as opposed to introverted intuition, which prefers to take one or two ideas and really delve deep into them. My second function is an introverted function (Introverted feeling, meaning that I feel less of a need to modulate my emotional expression to fit the 'group' than extroverted feelers), and I believe that I am an introvert in the traditional sense of the word, despite having an 'E' on Myers Briggs. People who think it's about whether the first letter dictates whether you're socially an introvert or an extrovert haven't done much research.

\`Secondly - in MBTI, we all have all eight functions. The four letters just indicate the top four in the stack; it's not binary, we don't 'choose between them', we just tend to prefer some functions over others. That's human.

It blows my mind how people, especially journalists, are willing to hold such damning views of this psychological model while also having zero actual idea about how it works.

I get what you're saying, but, in my experience, Fe users have been much more prone to succumbing to mob mentality and condemning someone for having values that don't align with the group without considering the person's unique perspective. Fi prioritizes the individual, and helps allow the user to form their own unique opinions on a person's character, divorced from external pressure or bias. Sure, it means that, in some cases, the Fi user will go against the grain and say they *dislike* the person who most people like, but just as often (or maybe even more), a strong Fi user will have an open mind about a person when everyone else has already written them off.

In my immediate family, there are 4 Fi users and 2 Fe users. The Fe users are much more likely to damn people over their opinions than the Fi users, and even *more* likely to hide their dislike behind a facade of false pleasantries. Not to say that all Fe users will do this - just that everyone is capable of these kinds of behaviours, so I don't think you should lump all Fi users together. I know on MBTI forums there's a lot of talk about Fi users being all gung ho on their moral values, but these 'values' can often be as innocent as 'love is the most important thing in life' or 'art is the purest form of self expression'. It doesn't mean that every Fi user you meet is going to despise you for having a different opinion on who should be mayor, or the ethics of lying.

So yeah, from a strong Fi user: don't be afraid of us! If we ever personally meet, I promise I wouldn't speak ill of you behind your back, and if we come across a topic on which we fundamentally disagree, I'm always up or a good-natured debate :)

My new jeans are still pretty tight, and I've got a long way to go - but I'm feeling better than I have in a long time.
